summary: Full published-paper red team finds two high-severity supplementary-target problems and one medium ownership conflict: a global closed analytic hypersurface is necessarily algebraic, geometric theta level does not justify full rational 16-torsion over the coordinate field, and the functional-transcendence route duplicates the accepted shared Part II. These findings do not disprove the principal existence theorem. Agent Codex, session codex-rtOQ9t; issue #5061; base 1487a97f4339cdb535733c234f4961b5dc8dc37d.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-MASSER-ZANNIER-20.result.json: item PAPER-MASSER-ZANNIER-20/66 and route 7; corresponding reader endpoint
findings.claim: For g >= 2 the claimed transcendental hypersurface cannot be a globally closed analytic hypersurface of A_g. The extraction promotes an unsupported local-to-global step into that theorem. Local or nonclosed analytic objects require a different statement.
findings.evidence: Masser–Zannier §5.4, pp. 669–670, is the source of the globalization. Le Fourn 6.4(a,b), printed p. 181, supplies the projective Satake compactification with boundary dimension G-g. For a hypersurface dim W=G-1>G-g. Demailly II(8.7), p. 118, extends its analytic closure across that boundary, including in a singular complex space; II(8.10), p. 121, makes the projective closure algebraic. Thus W is algebraic, contradicting the extracted transcendence property and the combination with item 58. The report provides the full argument and exact primary-source URLs.
findings.fix: Keep the real-analytic interpolation image separately. Record the failed globalization as a new source issue and gate the global endpoint in item 66, route 7 and the reader. State and prove a suitably local/germ or nonclosed replacement with its ambient domain explicit before enabling that replacement; do not claim a transcendental closed hypersurface in all A_g. Preserve the main algebraic hypersurface-avoidance theorem.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-MASSER-ZANNIER-20.result.json: items PAPER-MASSER-ZANNIER-20/56 and /58, route 7; reader discussion of rational 16-torsion
findings.claim: The full rational 16-torsion conclusion requires an arithmetic fine-level model and descent comparison absent from the planned inference from the complex congruence subgroup. A Q-model of the theta variety does not establish that every associated coordinate field trivializes the torsion; the distinction affects the target's field-degree bound.
findings.evidence: The inference occurs at the end of Masser–Zannier §5.2, p. 666. A perfect Galois-equivariant Weil pairing on a principally polarized A/K with all A[16] rational forces mu_16 into K, excluding real K. Le Fourn 6.5(b)/6.6(a), printed p. 182, places full symplectic level over Z[zeta_n,1/n]. The report gives a real-theta-coordinate diagnostic at tau=i I_g and distinguishes its coordinate-field obstruction from the still-possible extra existential torsion theorem.
findings.fix: Separate the theta coordinate model, arithmetic fine-level moduli/universal scheme, and torsion field. Prove their comparison using existing PELModuli M2/M5 and AbelianSchemes A3/A5 suppliers; account for cyclotomic and any further descent extensions in D(Atilde,Psi) and the final bound. Either prove the supplementary torsion conclusion with that bound or explicitly gate it as unresolved. Add a source issue and propagate it to items 56/58, route 7 and the reader. Do not assert that adjoining zeta_16 alone suffices or that Theorem 1.1 itself is false.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-MASSER-ZANNIER-20.result.json: items /19–/23, route 1 and route 7's imports; reader owner map
findings.claim: The LD.6 source route and planned statuses for functional-transcendence foundations conflict with LD.6's supplier-consuming contract and duplicate the accepted LogicAndDefinabilityPartII proposal. Deferring selection of a single owner leaves incompatible executable briefs.
findings.evidence: LD.6 constructs its applications from separate suppliers and requires independent functional-transcendence input. Accepted PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 route 1 and its review assign weakly special geometry, uniformization definability and functional transcendence to LogicAndDefinabilityPartII, importing only early LD.6 counting. The target's historical Tsimerman precedent is also superseded in the current file by a merged, still-review-pending fix; that pending fix is corroboration only, not the acceptance basis for this finding.
findings.fix: Keep items 16–18 and 38 at LD.6. Coalesce items 19–23 with the existing LogicAndDefinabilityPartII ID/parent/title, distinguish missing shared foundations from completed library work, and specify genus-one/Siegel adapters and a shared Ax–Lindemann deduction. Update route 7 and the reader to import this owner. Preserve early counting -> Part II -> arithmetic applications; do not add a whole-stage LD.6 cycle.
